summary: Verified the demand/ai_risk hardcoded-Polish-word bug fix. Backend: new pytest (test_iter51_demand_airisk_canonical.py) registers a DE-country user, sets ui_language=en, submits the exact profile from the request (Księgowa/Berlin), generates recommendations and asserts every career's 'demand' and 'ai_risk' field is exactly one of 'high'/'medium'/'low' — PASSED (all 10 careers canonical). Frontend: logged in as that same EN-interface user on the live matches screen — badges correctly render 'Demand: high', 'AI risk: medium', 'AI risk: low' etc. in English while job titles stayed German (Finanzbuchhalter/in, Controller/in...) and why/summary text in English — exactly per spec, zero raw tokens or Polish leakage. Logged in as existing Polish-interface user (ania_t1@test.pl) — badges show 'Popyt: średni' / 'Ryzyko AI: średnie' with correct Polish grammar (masculine for Popyt, neuter for Ryzyko AI). Light regression pass: quiz/recommendations language-country split (DE market + EN UI) re-confirmed working end-to-end alongside this fix, no new breakage observed.
action_items: None — fix verified working as intended, no regressions found.
critical_code_review_comments: LEVEL_WORDS/normalize_level() in server.py defaults unknown values to 'medium' (safe fallback) and covers pl/de/nl stray words plus the canonical en tokens — reasonable defensive normalization given LLM output variability.

Frontend levelLabel() in index.tsx correctly maps canonical token -> per-language, per-field (demand vs aiRisk) translated+inflected string via i18n; Polish file correctly differentiates masculine (wysoki/średni/niski) vs neuter (wysokie/średnie/niskie) forms — grammatically correct.

Note: pl-interface regression test only exercised 'medium' level (ania_t1's cached recommendations); did not observe live 'wysoki'/'niski'/'wysokie'/'niskie' forms in this session, but EN-equivalent high/medium/low tokens rendering correctly for the same component logic gives high confidence the Polish masculine/neuter mapping (verified via code read in pl.ts) is also correct.

rca_of_issue: N/A — this iteration verifies a fix, not a new bug.
